query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The dual‐phase eutectic high‐entropy alloy AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared to conventional duplex stainless steel under high-temperature molten salt conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in its as-cast dual-phase state with a mix of FCC and BCC/B2 phases exhibiting homogeneously distributed elements.
generation.intervention: Exposure to a high-temperature tribo-corrosion environment using a molten salt (NaCl-KCl-MgCl2) at temperatures of 450 °C and 650 °C.
generation.conditions: Molten salt environment at elevated temperatures (450 °C and 650 °C) to simulate conditions typical of advanced solar power or nuclear applications.
generation.structural_mediator: The dual-phase microstructure, where the FCC phase acts as a protective barrier and the BCC/B2 phase undergoes selective dissolution that induces micro-galvanic coupling, mediating passivation.
generation.mechanism: The formation of a surface layer enriched in noble elements from the FCC phase, which increases the work function and inhibits further oxidation, combined with the controlled selective dissolution of the BCC phase that minimizes overall material loss.
generation.predicted_outcome: The EHEA will show significantly lower corrosion rates (e.g., ~1 mm/year at 450 °C and ~9 mm/year at 650 °C) compared to duplex stainless steel (e.g., ~8 mm/year and ~20 mm/year, respectively), indicating improved resistance to tribo-corrosion degradation.
generation.baseline: Conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 tested under identical molten salt tribo-corrosion conditions.
generation.boundary: The superior performance is expected in environments where both elevated temperatures and corrosive molten salts are present; however, variations in processing or microstructural defects might affect the extent of improvement.
generation.uncertainty: Exact corrosion rates and the detailed contributions of micro-galvanic coupling are sensitive to specific processing parameters and environmental fluctuations, which require further experimental quantification.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a comparative corrosion study by subjecting samples of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA and DS2205 duplex stainless steel to identical molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt baths at 450 °C and 650 °C over a fixed time period. Measure mass loss, surface morphology (using SEM), phase distribution (using XRD), and surface potential differences (using a scanning Kelvin probe) before and after exposure.
measurements: Surface composition and phase changes via XRD and SEM
Volta potential differences via scanning Kelvin probe
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA does not show statistically significant lower corrosion rates or evidence of protective surface passivation compared to DS2205 under the same conditions, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract Dual-phase high entropy alloys have recently attracted widespread attention as advanced structural materials due to their unique microstructure, excellent mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance. However, their molten salt corrosion behavior has not been reported, which is critical in evaluating their application merit in the areas of concentrating solar power and nuclear energy. Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205). The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205. Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205. There was selective dissolution of the body-centered cubic phase in both the alloys, B2 in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and α-Ferrite in DS2205. This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.
